properties.disease overview: Fracture of the femoral diaphysis, typically from high-energy trauma (MVC, fall) but can also be pathological or stress-related; important due to major blood loss risk and adjacent neurovascular injury.
properties.mechanism: High-energy bending/axial/torsional forces cause diaphyseal fracture; strong surrounding muscle forces can displace fragments and contribute to shortening/angulation; significant intramedullary bleeding possible.
